newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia's Chiluba names cabinet for second term.
newsitem.headline: Zambia's Chiluba names cabinet for second term.

text.p: Zambian President Frederick Chiluba named a largely unchanged government for his second and final term on Monday, in which his chief advisors retained their old positions.

Chiluba, who won elections last month that the opposition said were rigged, kept Godfrey Miyanda as vice-president and kept his previous key minister without portfolio, Michael Sata, in the new government line-up he announced at a news conference.
Other members of the cabinet that retained their old positions include Defence Minister Ben Mwila, Home Affairs Minister Chitalu Sampa, and Finance Minister Ronald Penza.
Lawrence Shimba replaced Christon Tembo as foreign minister.
Tembo was transferred to the ministry of mines, replacing Keli Walubita, who moved to the ministry of works and supply.
Former Energy Minister Edith Nawakwi became the new Minister of Agriculture, exchanging portfolios with Suresh Desai.

Chiluba declined to bring back into power some key advisors -- former deputy speaker of the national assembly, Sikota Wina, his wife and former community development minister, Nakatindi Wina, and former foreign minister Vernon Mwaanga -- citing pressure from donor nations.
"These are some of the difficulties that poor nations like ours have to live with," Chiluba said.
"These people have been cleared of their allegations, but the strong feelings against them are, unfortunately, still in the minds of some people we cannot ignore," he added.
The Winas and Mwaanga were forced to resign their positions by donor pressure in early 1991 after persistent reports linking them to drug trafficking.
Western governments had threatened to cut aid to Zambia if Chiluba retained them in his government.
